title: Seeing Through the Sky
content: In his bookModern Painters, John Ruskin speaks of looking notata sky, butthroughit.“It is not flat dead colour, but a deep, quivering, transparent body of penetrable air, in which you trace or imagine short falling spots of deceiving light, and dim shades, faint veiled vestiges of dark vapour.”Painting:Thomas Hill(1829-1908), View of Yosemite Valley, 1871.
